incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008: ss.12 (incorporation), 13 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 14 (Notice of Incorporation), 19 (separate legal personality), 40 (consideration for shares), 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR14.1) and Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) filed through CIPC e-Services
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Proprietary Limited company; no escrow account is mandated. Shares may be issued for no par value or deferred consideration, subject to the solvency and liquidity test in s40(1) of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the sole incorporator/subscribers, that the company be and is hereby incorporated as ZA_PTY_LTD (Proprietary) Limited under the Companies Act 71 of 2008; that the draft Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation are approved and submitted to CIPC; that shares be subscribed and allotted in accordance with the MOI, with payment deferred in terms of s40(1); that the registered office be adopted at [address]; that Jane Doe is appointed as sole Director and John Doe as Company Secretary, each to serve until removed in accordance with the MOI. All actions taken by directors to give effect hereto are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application to CIPC using the e-Services online portal, entering at least two proposed company names in order of preference. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee and await the outcome. Once reserved, the name is held for the statutory validity period pending filing of the Notice of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed account profile authorization or agent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged for conflict/offensiveness, submit a fresh name reservation application with new proposed names within the outstanding validity period; no substantive company filing is required until a valid reservation is obtained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) setting out the constitution, share classes, director powers, and any pre-emption or governance restrictions. Complete Form CoR14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) including the registered office address and the names and consent of initial directors and officers.
required_dossiers: Written consents of initial directors and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of a CIPC compliance query or rejected MOI, remedy the specific drafting defect, amend the MOI or CoR14.1, and re-submit through the same CIPC e-Services channel; keep a copy of the rejection notice to maintain continuity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Payment of Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed CoR14.1, MOI, and supporting consents to CIPC e-Services, pay the official filing fee, and formally submit the incorporation application. Monitor the filing status and obtain the electronic or physical Certificate of Incorporation once the application is approved.
required_dossiers: Final MOI signed by all incorporators
Certified ID/passport copies of incorporators and initial directors
Proof of CIPC filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC issues a query or rejection notice, correct the formal defects indicated, resubmit the affected form or MOI, and pay any shortfall within the stated CIPC deadline; expedited escalation is available through the CIPC contact center or physical walk-in branch if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution, Share Subscription and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial board of directors / subscribers (corporate record action)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the pro-forma board resolution approving the share subscription, allotment of shares to subscribers, adoption of the registered office address, and appointment of directors and company secretary as set out in the MOI. Keep signed minutes and share registers in the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting and board resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first board meeting is invalid for lack of quorum or defective notice, convene an adjourned meeting on proper notice and ratify all prior actions by unanimous written shareholder consent in accordance with the MOI and Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SARS, UIF and Compensation Fund Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a taxpayer with SARS and obtain an income tax reference number; register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed the compulsory threshold; register for Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE), UIF, and Skills Development Levy if employees will be appointed. File the relevant declarations through SARS eFiling and register with the Compensation Fund for COIDA compliance.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or proof of address
Bank account details or banking letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS sends a bracketing letter or requests additional documents, respond through eFiling within the specified timeline, provide the corrected information, and, if needed, obtain a tax clearance or VAT letter via the SARS branch or e-service portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Premises Compliance, Occupational Health and Safety and Fire Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal planning and licensing department; municipal fire authority; Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the zoning rights of the registered office and obtain an occupancy certificate or municipal trading/business licence if the local by-laws require it. Arrange for a structural load assessment where server racks or heavy equipment are installed, obtain a fire safety certificate from the local fire department, and register any workplace with the Compensation Fund under the Occupational Health and Safety Act. Implement an emergency evacuation plan and electrical certificate of compliance.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of premises ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority or fire department raises non-compliance, abate the identified defect, obtain revised certificates, and apply for the relevant clearance or license through the municipal one-stop-shop; appeal any refusal under the applicable by-law appeal mechanism.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of Trade, Industry and Competition (dtic) and Municipal Planning/Licensing Department; ICASA is not engaged because the activity is unlicensed software-based advertising, not a broadcasting or OTT content service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence or Occupancy Certificate for commercial premises (where applicable), combined with compliance certificates under the Occupational Health and Safety Act; no separate statutory AdTech operating license is required for the programmatic advertising exchange platform

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt / Low-Risk for a purely office-based technology operation; a Basic Assessment Report may be triggered only if physical infrastructure development (e.g. data centre or listed stormwater/electrical works) is added to the registered premises under the EIA Regulations, 2014
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the National Water Act and municipal sewer by-laws for any domestic wastewater; standby diesel generators, if installed, must meet atmospheric emission limits under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act; waste electrical and electronic equipment must be handled under the National Waste Management Act and e-waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and building occupancy certificate issued by the local municipal fire/emergency and building control authorities; structural load inspection for server/equipment floor loading; electrical certificate of compliance; occupational health and safety registration with the Department of Employment and Labour under the OHS Act 85 of 1993; emergency evacuation plan and personal protective equipment protocol for maintenance areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); national filing and registration portal: SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd must submit the Company Registration Application via SARS eFiling or the COR101 form at the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) to obtain a SARS Income Tax Reference Number. VAT registration is lodged on Form VAT101 within 21 days of crossing the compulsory R1,000,000 annual taxable turnover threshold, supported by certified memorandum of incorporation, directors' identification, local registered office proof, and shareholding disclosures. The resulting vendor number (VAT reference number) is distinct from the income tax reference number, and both are consolidated under the same SARS eFiling profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A South African-resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed on worldwide income at the 27% corporate income tax rate (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023), with no territorial exemption and no tax-exempt-zone status applicable to standard advertising/AdTech operations. Dividend distributions attract the 20% dividends tax withheld at source. The entity is treated as a separate taxpayer from its shareholders; no look-through or pass-through treatment is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification regime. Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT grouping election under section 50 of the VAT Act for commonly controlled entities; (ii) consolidated group taxation election under section 41 of the Income Tax Act at a 72% common-ownership threshold (deemed single tax entity); and (iii) voluntary VAT registration election upon turnover exceeding R50,000 in 12 months. Hybrid mismatch rules under sections 23M to 24I apply mandatorily without an opt-out election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (ZAR) taxable supplies in the preceding 12-month rolling period for compulsory registration; R50,000 (ZAR) voluntary registration threshold for small vendors
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate, or digital stamping is currently in force in South Africa. Taxpayers file VAT returns via SARS eFiling (periodic, typically bi-monthly); standard compliant VAT invoices are acceptable. SARS has published a draft e-invoicing framework and continues to issue public discussion papers, but no statutory API-based clearance or pre-clearance approval obligation applies for the 2025 compliance year.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act when goods are physically exported from South Africa by the vendor or by the purchaser within the prescribed period and the vendor retains proof of export. Services: section 11(2)(l) zero-rates services supplied to a non-resident recipient (including offshore programmatic ad DSP/SSP platform services) where the services are not supplied for use or consumption in South Africa; the provider must hold a written contract identifying the non-resident recipient and demonstrating no local consumption. AdTech platform fees paid by foreign publishers/advertisers into South Africa generally qualify for zero-rating when the service recipient is outside the common customs area and the intellectual property/SSP service is not used for trade within South Africa.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SARS Customs Export Declaration (SAD500) with unique customs clearance reference

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure of goods from South Africa within 120 days of the time of supply (goods), or for services: signed offshore service purchase agreement and non-resident recipient confirmation
Commercial Invoice / Tax Invoice issued at 0% VAT
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or underlying SWIFT wire/foreign exchange recording confirming receipt of export proceeds into a South African bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may audit and claw back unlawfully claimed zero-rated output VAT, demanding additional 15% output tax plus interest from the date the supply was reported, and may disallow input credits under section 16(4) where substantiation is deficient. Understatement penalties under section 222 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 range from 10% to 150% of the shortfall depending on conduct (substantial non-compliance, negligence, or intentional tax evasion); false invoices or reckless misstatements may additionally attract a criminal offense under section 234/235 with imprisonment up to five years, reputational sanctions, and full restitution of VAT, penalties, and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB); exchange control is administered by the SARB Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) as delegate of the Minister of Finance under the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961, read with the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers. The National Payment System is also overseen by SARB under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The rand is fully convertible for current-account transactions and selectively convertible for capital-account transactions. A South African resident company may remit dividends, service fees, royalties, and operational payments abroad through an Authorised Dealer without prior FinSurv approval, provided the payment is supported by the underlying commercial documentation, a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN, and for dividends a declaration complying with the Companies Act 71 of 2008 solvency/liquidity test and the 20% dividends withholding tax regime. Capital-account inflows and outflows, including inward foreign equity, shareholder loans, and offshore treasury arrangements, must be recorded with the receiving Authorised Dealer under the FinSurv reporting architecture and are subject to purpose-of-payment classification; larger external loan facilities require either FinSurv approval or Authorised Dealer exercised authority under the prevailing external-loan threshold limits contained in the Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers. Profit repatriation is not prohibited, but banks will block remittances if the beneficial owner chain is opaque, the SARS tax compliance status is invalid, or the underlying economic substance of the AdTech activities cannot be substantiated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All proceeds from exported services rendered by the South African (Pty) Ltd to non-resident DSP, SSP, and programmatic advertising counterparties must be received in South Africa within 180 days from the date of performance or invoice due date, whichever is earlier, unless an extended collection period is approved by the FinSurv or the Authorised Dealer. Upon receipt in foreign currency, the proceeds must be surrendered to an Authorised Dealer within 30 days, meaning they must be converted into rand through the banking system at the ruling market rate and credited to the entity's rand operational account, unless the exporter holds a FinSurv-sanctioned foreign-currency account retention facility permitting the full or partial retention of qualifying export proceeds for subsequent commercial use. The financial institution will apply the standard export-control verification protocols, including confirmation of the commercial invoice, the matching SWIFT credit advice, and the maintenance of a service-export register to demonstrate timely repatriation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as a supplementary settlement and FX channel; Low as a primary bank relationship. A foreign or offshore digital EMI, including an EU-licensed e-money institution, is not a deposit-taking institution in South Africa and cannot operate a rand-based clearing account for the South African entity without a local sponsorship arrangement with a licensed South African bank participating in the BankservAfrica national payment system. The (Pty) Ltd may lawfully use a compliant international EMI to collect small-balance programmatic advertising receipts from non-resident ad networks, but all rand liquidity must ultimately be aggregated and swept into a domestic commercial bank account to satisfy SARB exchange control and FIC Act obligations. Contractual terms with the EMI must provide for full client-fund segregation, transaction monitoring, and SARB-compliant purpose-of-payment disclosure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence for account opening is the practical standard across the four major banks. At least one authorised director and the designated financial officer must attend a face-to-face onboarding interview at a South African branch, or submit to a bank-initiated on-site visit at the company's registered offices, to verify identity documents, source of funds, and operational genuineness. Remote onboarding is rarely accepted for a new legal entity with non-resident connected parties; where permitted, it requires video-linked identification, independent notarisation of the board resolution, apostilled corporate documentation, and a compliance committee override. The bank will also require two or more mandated signatories under one-for-one or dual-control authority, and none of the signatories may be resident outside South Africa without prior Authorised Dealer approval for offshore mandate execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity programmatic advertising flows involving thousands of low-value bid-level transactions from non-face-to-face DSP and SSP counterparties, which can resemble money laundering or unidentifiable third-party receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provision of a granular fund-flow diagram showing bid request, auction, ad exchange, clearing house, and final settlement legs; a whitelist of approved commercial counterparties with jurisdiction, legal entity, and bank account details; aggregated monthly transaction reports by platform; signed DSP/SSP master services agreements; audited trail of invoices matched to unique transaction reference numbers; and a compliance policy manual confirming transaction screening, threshold reporting, and source-of-funds verification per transaction cohort.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership where the ultimate parent or treasury centre is offshore, especially if the shareholding chain passes through tax-favourable jurisdictions or trust-like structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC certificate of incorporation and annual returns; full group structure chart identifying all natural-person beneficial owners with percentage holdings; a FIC Act compliant beneficial ownership register; apostilled or notarised certificates of incumbency for each intermediate entity; board resolution of the South African company approving the account mandate; and a FATF-aligned legal opinion from South African counsel classifying the ownership structure as low risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commingling of capital escrow proceeds with operational trading funds, creating ambiguity over the source and intended use of cleared liquidity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow and account-segregation agreement; separate Capital Escrow Account and Operational Transactional Account with dedicated IBAN-equivalent account numbers; monthly independent accountant's assurance report mapping all escrow movements; reconciliation of subscriber/advertiser balances against crowd-funded or investor capital records; and board-approved treasury policy prohibiting inter-account netting without documentary support.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ad-network settlement payments that do not match the invoiced value of services, raising concerns of over-invoicing, receipt of unidentifiable third-party funds, or disguised capital inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Compliance Status PIN; signed commercial agreements with each ad network; per-settlement invoice reconciliation report matched against SWIFT MT103 field 70 remittance information; a service-export register identifying the nature of services rendered; internal logs of ad delivery metrics and SSP clearing statements; and a copy of the Authorised Dealer export-control verification form where required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 COV in USD, EUR, GBP, or ZAR to the (Pty) Ltd's Capital Escrow Account at a licensed South African Authorised Dealer. The remitter must state the SARB/FinSurv purpose-of-payment category, which for ordinary non-resident equity subscriptions is the direct-investment equity capital category, and for shareholder loans is the other-investment loan category; the receiving bank will screen the transfer against FinSurv loan-approval thresholds and record the inward transfer in the FinSurv reporting system. Verification requires submission of the board resolution approving the capital injection, the subscription or loan agreement, a certificate of the foreign shareholder's due incorporation, and a confirmation that the funds will be applied for the working-capital and platform-expansion purposes disclosed in the compliance file. Any subsequent return of capital, redemption, or interest remittance to the non-resident shareholder must be routed through the same Authorised Dealer with matching purpose codes and tax directives.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for programmatic advertising inventory, data fees, and publisher revenue shares will be executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers and, for bank-to-bank treasury movements, MT202 COV. Where the foreign publisher or SSP counterparty requires security, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued under ICC UCP 600 using an MT700 SWIFT message may be used, normally subject to presentation of a clearing statement or invoice. Rand-denominated domestic disbursements to South African publishers and vendors will be cleared through the BankservAfrica electronic fund transfer (EFT/ACH Direct) system using the automated clearing house. The treasury desk will maintain segregated currency accounts, daily liquidity forecasting, and a release matrix under dual-authorisation to ensure every outbound payment matches an underlying commercial obligation and carries the correct SARB purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts (FECs) concluded with an Authorised Dealer against a documented underlying commercial transaction
Cross-currency swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps for matching long-term USD revenue with ZAR operating costs
Option-based structures, including European-style FX options, limited to hedging of an existing or anticipated underlying exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) arranged through a domestic Authorised Dealer, where economically necessary for rand or offshore-currency exposure management, but never on a speculative or uncovered basis

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023; reduced from 28% for the 2022/23 year of assessment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday regime; available preferential deductions include the s11D R&D additional 50% deduction (150% total), s12B/12BA accelerated and 125%/100% renewable-energy capital allowances, s12H learnership allowances, s12E graduated Small Business Corporation rates (0%–27%), and the s6quat foreign-tax credit avoiding double taxation.
